✍️ Gaming Industry Trends & Market Insights

Generational Shift in Platforms and Technology: Testing the Vitality of IPs

How does the market react when popular, long-loved IPs meet new devices and the latest engines? 🔄
We analyze next-generation survival strategies that go beyond simple porting to make gamers open their wallets once again.
Recently, the gaming industry has faced a technological transition period to maximize the lifespan of existing IPs. Key examples of this trend include Netmarble's 'Blade & Soul Revolution' undergoing an unprecedented engine upgrade to Unreal Engine 5 (UE5) for a mobile game, and Square Enix's decision to release a next-generation console (Switch 2) version of 'Dragon Quest XI S'. 🎮

These moves fundamentally change consumers' game consumption structure. Instead of searching for new games every time, players now expect the existing IPs in which they have invested time and money to be fully preserved in the latest platforms and high-end graphic environments. Although this imposes an additional development cost burden on game companies to adapt to next-generation devices, it acts as a key lock-in effect, preventing the departure of the existing loyal customer base and maintaining stable revenue streams. 📈

Ultimately, a game company's 'ability to port existing assets in a future-oriented manner' has become as crucial a core competency as new game development in determining its sustainability. In a cycle of rapid generational shifts in technology and hardware, a hybrid service capability that respects the value accumulated by players and smoothly connects it to the next level is the key to long-term success. 🔑

Whether technological progress will be a blessing that extends the lifespan of existing titles or a shackle that only adds to development costs depends on sophisticated porting and optimization strategies. Is the game you hold dear ready to survive on the upcoming next-generation platforms? 🤔
— Dr. K
